newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France to drop Paris-Teheran route.
newsitem.headline: Air France to drop Paris-Teheran route.

text.p: French flag-carrier Air France said on Tuesday it would drop its Paris-Teheran flight next month because it was losing money.
"We have decided for reasons of profitability to drop this route from September 14," an Air France spokesman said, confirming a report in business daily, La Tribune.

"We will in future maintain a sales office with five employees in Teheran. This route was loss-making for us," he said. He gave no details of the scale of losses other than to say it was hard to make money with one flight a week which was on average only 70 percent full.
La Tribune said the airline believed "the Iranian authorities hampered the service by not allowing fares from Teheran to be set freely.

"Like other western airlines operating in this country, Air France can no longer repatriate local revenues and as with other European competitors (Lufthansa, British Airways Plc, Swissair, Austrian Airlines and Alitalia ), it has suffered sharp rent increases, and fees for flights and landings have more than doubled since 1993," the report said.
Iranian embassy officials said they were not aware of the situation.
The French Foreign Ministry said Air France did not need government approval for dropping a route as such a decision was a commercial one. Transport Ministry officials were not available for comment.
The company did not rule out resuming the service if economic conditions improved, the spokesman said.
